Name: CLI Mod Manager
Author: Pharaok
Description:
[size=2]It will enable the mods it found in the config file(s) you passed, and disable everything else.[/size]
[size=2]disabled mods will be moved to Mods_disabled inside your stardew valley directory.
If it doesn't find a mod you wanted to enable, it'll ignore it.
[/size]
[size=6]Config files:[/size]
Config files are just txt files with the mods you want to use on each line

example:[code]ConsoleCommands
SaveBackup
﻿CJBCheatsMenu
CJBItemSpawner
[/code]

[size=6]Usage:[/size]
[list=1]
[*]Open your command line
[*]Type in
[code]cd the/mod/manager/directory/[/code]
and hit enter
[*]The application's usage is:
[code]﻿./SDVModManager (--path=<path> | --steam | --gog) <config-files>...
[/code]
if you don't have a default path as seen [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Player_Guide/Getting_Started#Find_your_game_folder]here[/url],
you will have to specify the full path with --path﻿=your/stardew/valley/path.
[color=#ffff00][size=2]Important note﻿: [/size][/color][size=2]if any of your paths have spaces, please put them in quotation marks.

[/size]Arguments can be abbreviated, e.g. -p instead of --path, -s instead of --steam, -g instead of --gog.
Keep in mind that if you use -p to not type = as that will be used as part of your path.
[/list]example: 
[code]﻿cd D:/modManager
[/code][code]./SDVmodManager --path="D:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Stardew Valley" cjb.txt qol.txt global.txt
[/code]
[size=2]If you're going to be frequently﻿ switching between the same sets of mods, I recommend looking into batch/shell/command scripts.[/size]
I might make an UI for it in the future, but probably not any time soon.
